name: Security Incidents
blurb:
This section tracks open incidents reported on the status pages of 12 AI infrastructure and model providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Lambda, Fireworks AI, Baseten, Deepgram, and ElevenLabs. It counts how many incidents each provider has open at a given time, not a curated list of disclosed security breaches, so it works as an operational health signal rather than a security news feed. Status pages are checked multiple times a day and logged daily, giving a running count back to mid-August 2026.

Because it draws on provider-published status pages, it will catch outages and provider-declared incidents, but it will miss anything a company does not post to its own status page, including disclosed vulnerabilities, data exposures, or research findings about model behavior. Read it as a proxy for provider reliability stress, not as a security-incident archive.

As of September 5, 2026, the tracker shows zero open incidents across all 12 providers, following a quieter stretch since late August. The busiest period was August 14 through 25, when 2 to 4 incidents were open concurrently most days, peaking at 4 on August 24. Lambda has been the most incident-prone provider by far, with incidents flagged on 62 of 142 checks, about 44 percent, versus 21 of 148 for OpenAI, 14 percent, and 18 of 148 for Fireworks AI, 12 percent. Cohere, Anthropic, Baseten, and Deepgram each cleared over 97 percent of checks incident-free.

reading.body:
Lambda's infrastructure shows materially higher operational stress than peers, recording incidents on 44 percent of checks versus 12-14 percent for OpenAI and Fireworks AI, signaling either scale strain or reliability gaps in a critical compute-access layer.

The August 14-25 spike, with 2-4 concurrent incidents most days and a peak of 4, suggests the infrastructure providers serving AI development faced genuine strain during that period. This matters because AI training and inference runs depend on uninterrupted access to compute. When these platforms go down, work stops. The subsequent quiet stretch through early September points to either relief from that pressure or improved stability, though the data does not distinguish between them.

This tracker captures only incidents posted to provider status pages. It will miss security vulnerabilities, data exposures, or model behavior problems that companies do not publicly declare. It also does not measure severity, duration, or customer impact, only whether something was flagged as open. Read it as a real-time proxy for infrastructure reliability stress, not as a comprehensive security record.

The variance between providers is sharp. Cohere, Anthropic, Baseten, and Deepgram each cleared over 97 percent of checks incident-free. Lambda's 44 percent incident rate stands apart, raising questions about why one infrastructure provider diverges so far from the others operating in the same ecosystem.
